thought.text: Let me make the backup location safer (in case node's `/usr/local/lib` copy interferes):

reasoning_content:
The backup file is at `/usr/local/lib/libapk.so.3.0.0.base`, and the node copy overwrites `/usr/local/lib`... no wait, `COPY --from=node /usr/local/lib /usr/local/lib` copies node's /usr/local/lib to /usr/local/lib. Does node's /usr/local/lib contain libapk? No, node's libapk is in /usr/lib. But the node image's /usr/local/lib might have other stuff. The `.base` file is inside /usr/local/lib — when node's /usr/local/lib gets copied over /usr/local/lib, Docker's COPY doesn't delete existing files, it just overwrites what's there. My backup file will remain (unless node has a file with the same name — it won't). But just to be safe, let's move the backup to /tmp instead... Actually, /tmp inside a build stage might get cleared? No, there's no cleaning between RUN/COPY steps within a stage. But it would be safer to put it in /usr/share, or to simply restore before copying node's /usr/local/lib. A better approach: restore right after copying node's /usr/lib, and put the backup in /usr/local/etc (less likely to be overwritten). Let me restructure: put the backup at /usr/local/etc/libapk.so.3.0.0.base.

Let me fix it.

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "cd /workspace && sed -i 's|/usr/local/lib/libapk.so.3.0.0.base|/usr/local/etc/libapk.so.3.0.0.base|g' docker/tooling/tooling.Dockerfile && grep -n 'libapk' docker/tooling/tooling.Dockerfile", "security_risk": "MEDIUM", "summary": "Move libapk backup to safer path"}

summary: Move libapk backup to safer path
